to: the socket that the server disconnects next; for a shutdown, every socket (`broadcast`)

confirm.note: Every emit passes a string literal except `shutdown`, which passes `data.reason` with no type check.

variants.name: Call cost
variants.when: The call cost of the socket went above its limit. `limitdcreport` comes first.

variants.name: Limits from the web server
variants.when: `enforce_limitations` on the web server: too many characters for one IP address or one account. A merchant counts on its own.

variants.name: Blocked
variants.when: `block_account` on the web server: an admin blocks the account. Each character of the account gets it.

variants.name: Loose connections
variants.when: A new socket connects and more than 5 sockets without a character, the new one included, have the same IP address. Each older socket without a character gets this text.
variants.example: Too many loose connections from your network. Simply reload to play.

confirm.note: `is_socket_allowed` counts the new socket too: it is in `sockets` already.

variants.name: Shutdown
variants.when: An admin sends `shutdown` with a `reason`. The text is that reason. The server stops 10 s later.

confirm.note: `data.reason` is not checked: any truthy JSON value from the admin is sent as is.

variants.name: Check-in (dead code)
variants.when: Never: the code is inside an `if (0 && ...)` block.
variants.example: Failed to check in. Your network might be too slow.

senders.what: The wrapper of every handler: the call-cost check, and the check after a handler error.
